summary: CKGSB's global marketing team is pivoting to prioritize China-based programs Asia Star and Intelligent China for SEO/AI-search visibility, while finalizing the Knowledge website redesign and resolving a lingering Outlook lockout.
summaryDetail: The top priority is the new global marketing strategy: Asia Star and Intelligent China are now the lead programs for SEO and AI-search visibility, with US partner programs (Stanford, Columbia, Berkeley) secondary. This week, Joseph must draft the target areas/prompts and audience focus document and profile existing Asia Star participants and CRM hot leads, while the team obtains the conversion tracking brief and audits the setup. The Knowledge website redesign is moving forward with the current design retained, menu categorization as the key improvement, and Joseph's editorial layout inspiring more article display and indices (BCI, BSI) on the homepage; Joseph shares the HTML concept, then a 30-minute working session with Julie and the team lead will mark specific feedback before Joker implements changes. Urgent housekeeping: the team must resolve the Outlook account lockout by deleting and re-adding email accounts, updating saved passwords on all devices, and checking home devices for stale credentials. Looking ahead, upcoming actions include promoting Andrea and Katya spotlight videos, sending the SwissCham cooperation email for the 2026 Sino-Swiss Economic Forum, attending the European Chamber Silver Economy event, and sharing English case studies.

decisions.text: Account lockout was caused by stale saved passwords repeatedly hitting the backend; unlock already done.
Keep the current Knowledge design rather than a dramatic revamp, with menu categorization as the main improvement.
Remove the standalone videos section and disperse videos by topic instead.
Use Joseph's editorial-style layout as inspiration to display more articles and bring indices (BCI, BSI) to the Knowledge homepage.
Do not add a stock-market ticker at the top of the homepage.
Keep the school menu at top right in gray and center the knowledge menu.
Asia Star and Intelligent China are the top two program priorities; US partner programs (Stanford, Columbia, Berkeley) are secondary for now.
Berkeley is the preferred third priority among US programs, to be considered in the audit phase.
Removed the figure 247 from the MBA new intake social media post to align with MBA's own WeChat channel
